title: Supreme Court Upholds Repudiation of Rs. 2.4 Crore Fire Claim Over False Stock Declaration
case_name: M/s New India Assurance Company Ltd. v. M/s Hemkund Duplex and Board Pvt. Ltd.
card_summary: The NCDRC had directed New India Assurance to pay Rs. 2.4 crore on two fire policies, disregarding the statutory surveyors' reports. The Supreme Court set that order aside, holding the Commission cannot brush aside surveyor findings without identifying a specific flaw. It found the insured had falsely shown usable raw material as destroyed, breaching policy conditions and justifying repudiation.
card_tip: A consumer forum cannot override a statutory surveyor's report on a bare disagreement; any challenge to repudiation must identify a concrete flaw in the survey, not just a different damage estimate.
verification_notes: The citation 2026 INSC 1023, the 21 September 2026 decision date, the bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva, the Rs. 2.4 crore figure, the false stock declaration finding, and the setting aside of the NCDRC's order are consistent across LiveLaw's and Verdictum's reports. The judgment text itself was not independently retrieved.
